races.title: State Assembly, District 65
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Ayanna Davis
cands.bio: Dr. Ayanna Davis is a Compton educator. She was a classroom teacher and a Los Angeles Unified School District early-education principal. She served on the Compton Unified School District board (Area B) from 2022 to 2026. She is the Democratic member-elect for Assembly District 65.

endorsements.text: Endorsed by the Democratic Party of California and Equality California, per Ballotpedia's endorsement list.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Ayanna Davis was born or when her family settled in California; her campaign site says only that she grew up in Compton. We found no votes, bills or official actions by her on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or school choice. We also found no stated positions from her on those topics. Her campaign site lists priority headings (education, housing and homelessness, public safety, jobs, healthcare, environment, civil rights) without detail. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022 or 2026. We found no documented statements from her on data centers or development, and no controversies or foreign ties. The Wikipedia page is a one-line stub and added nothing.

local.label: Roots 90: Her campaign site says she grew up in a single-parent home in Compton and still lives there, but it does not give her birthplace.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Teacher, then principal of two early education centers in Los Angeles Unified School District. Served on the Compton Unified School District board from 2022 to 2026, including as the board's legislative representative, according to her campaign site.
qual.why: She has held local elected office and worked as a school administrator, which fits the middle band. The sources show no prior legislative service or state budget or policy career.

cands.name: Lydia A. Gutiérrez
cands.bio: Educator and Republican candidate for Assembly District 65. Former teacher with 25+ years of experience. She worked as an aerospace administrator and a cost estimating supervisor. She served seven years as an elected member of the Coastal San Pedro Neighborhood Council. She has not held a legislative office.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements and voter-guide recommendations listed by Ballotpedia include Reform California, April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide, and The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn.
In her 2015 LAUSD race she was endorsed by the Los Angeles County Republican Party and the evangelical Christian group Election Forum.

cands.gaps: We could not find where she was born or raised, or when she came to California. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2026, and we found no 2026 campaign platform, so her stated positions on housing, property taxes, data centers, immigration, guns, abortion, policing and school choice are not documented here. We found no record of deeds in office on those topics, since she has never held a voting office. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties, or statements on data centers or development. Her only available platform text is from her 2015 school board campaign, and it does not address these topics.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Teacher for 25+ years, aerospace industry administrator, and cost estimating supervisor in a tank parts division. She served on the Coastal San Pedro Neighborhood Council for seven years. She has never held legislative office; she lost races for state Senate, Superintendent of Public Instruction, LAUSD board, community college board and Assembly.
qual.why: She has no legislative service and no policy or law career. Her cost-estimating supervisory work has some budget relevance. Her teaching career is not directly related to the office, and a neighborhood council seat counts as a civic board.
